title: Mirror Tree Check
statement:
You are given the root of a binary tree. Determine whether the tree is a mirror image of itself when reflected across a vertical axis through its root, that is, whether the left subtree is a mirror reflection of the right subtree.

Formally, two subtrees are mirror-symmetric if:
1. Both are empty, or
2. Both are non-empty, their root values are equal, the left child of the first subtree is a mirror match for the right child of the second subtree, and the right child of the first is a mirror match for the left child of the second.

Each node in the tree holds an integer value. You must return true if the whole tree exhibits this left-right mirror symmetry, and false otherwise. You may solve this using either a recursive traversal or an iterative approach with an explicit queue or stack.

examples.explanation:
The tree looks like:
        4
       / \
      7   7
     / \ / \
    3  5 5  3
Comparing the two subtrees rooted at the children of 4: values 7 and 7 match, then (3,5) on one side mirrors (5,3) on the other, so the whole tree is symmetric.

The tree looks like:
      2
     / \
    6   6
     \   \
      8   8
Although both 6-nodes match and both have a single child with value 8, the 8 under the left 6 is a right child while the 8 under the right 6 is also a right child, for a true mirror, one should be a left child and the other a right child. So the tree is not symmetric.

constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is in the range [0, 2000]
The tree structure is a standard binary tree (each node has at most two children, left and right)
